body.statement: Lemma (finite equality certificates).  If \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0\), then there are finite real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identities over a finite real algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\) certifying that \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\).  If the extension and every polynomial and product in those identities are supplied in expanded exact form, with exponents in unary, deterministic exact verification is polynomial in the total expanded certificate length.
body.justification: A termination theorem is meaningful only when both branches carry finite, size-accounted certificates.
body.gap: Existing effective real-algebraic bounds do not instantiate the complete expanded certificate contract for these rational causal circuits.
body.consumer: Independent proof checkers can validate equality outputs without trusting the computer-algebra system that produced them.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(R_0=\mathbb Q[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) and \(L=J_{\mathcal I}:s^{\infty}\), and fix \(D\in\mathfrak D\) and an outcome cell \(y\).  The defining property of reduction by the canonical reduced basis is
\[
 \operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}. \tag{5}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}saturated\text{-}real\text{-}radical}\), the right side of (5) says that \(F_{D,y}\) vanishes on the real variety of \(L\).  Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}real\text{-}nullstellensatz}\) after scalar extension to \(\mathbb R\).  There are an integer \(a\geq1\), finitely many \(q_i\in\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega]\), and an element \(h\in L\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) such that
\[
 F_{D,y}^{\,2a}+\sum_iq_i^2=h. \tag{6}
\]
Ideal membership in (6) has a finite representation
\[
 h=\sum_{\nu=1}^k b_\nu\ell_\nu,
 \qquad
 b_\nu\in\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega],
 \quad \ell_\nu\in L. \tag{7}
\]
For every \(\nu\), the definition of saturation supplies \(N_\nu\geq0\) with \(s^{N_\nu}\ell_\nu\in J_{\mathcal I}\).  Taking \(N=\max_\nu N_\nu\) and multiplying (6) by \(s^N\) therefore yields membership in the explicitly finitely generated ideal \(J_{\mathcal I}\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega]\).  If \(f_1,\ldots,f_r\) are its rational generators, there are \(a_j\in\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) for which
\[
 s^N\left(F_{D,y}^{\,2a}+\sum_iq_i^2\right)
   =\sum_{j=1}^r a_jf_j. \tag{8}
\]

Fix the integers \(a,N,k,r\) and all finite monomial supports occurring in one solution of (8).  Equating coefficients in (8) is then a finite existential sentence in the unknown coefficients of the \(q_i\) and \(a_j\), with rational coefficients.  It is true in \(\mathbb R\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}transfer}\), it is true in the real algebraic closure \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) of \(\mathbb Q\).  Thus all coefficients in (8) may be chosen in \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).  The finitely many coefficients generate a finite real algebraic extension \(E/\mathbb Q\).

Identity (8) is both the real-Nullstellensatz and saturation certificate.  Indeed, let \(r\) be a real point at which every generator of \(J_{\mathcal I}\) vanishes and \(s(r)\neq0\).  Evaluating (8) and dividing by \(s(r)^N\), which is permitted by the displayed nonvanishing condition, gives
\[
 F_{D,y}(r)^{2a}+\sum_iq_i(r)^2=0. \tag{9}
\]
All summands in (9) are nonnegative in the selected real embedding of \(E\), so \(F_{D,y}(r)=0\).  This is exactly the advertised vanishing consequence.

It remains to account for verification size.  Encode \(E\) by a primitive element, its square-free defining polynomial, and rational isolating or Thom data for the selected real root; encode every coefficient in the power basis.  The certificate also supplies every polynomial and every product in (8) in expanded form.  A checker uses exact rational polynomial arithmetic to verify the algebraic-number representation, reduces coefficient products modulo the defining polynomial, recomputes the advertised polynomial products, and compares the two expanded coefficient maps.  If \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}\) is the total expanded input length, the number of coefficient operations is bounded by a quadratic polynomial in \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}\); unary exponents ensure that repeated powering requires at most \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}\) advertised multiplications, and the bit lengths of sums and products are polynomial in the total bit length of their supplied operands.  Sturm or subresultant sign checks for the isolating data are likewise polynomial in the displayed degrees and coefficient bit lengths.  Hence deterministic exact verification is polynomial in \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  This is a verifier bound only; the argument asserts no uniform bound on the shortest certificate or on the time needed to find it.
